text_fidelity_a:
AuviPal G10 Backlit 2.4GHz Wireless Air Mouse Remote with Shortcut Keys, QWERTY Keyboard and Build-in Rechargeable Battery for Windows 10 PC Laptop Tablet Win10 Mini PC Stick HTPC Sigh, this one was a disappointment from the git go. After charging the remote and plugging in the wifi dongle, the first thing I did was hit the power button on the remote, intending to turn it on to pair it with the dongle. Nope, the power button shut down my whole computer even as the dongle was starting to download the necessary driver. Once I got the computer, a Windows 10 desktop, restarted, I couldn't tell if the driver had been installed or not. The mouse did not seem to be working at all. The keyboard did produce some results but they seemed to be random. The keys did unexpected, sometimes inexplicable things.

The instructions did give a couple of buttons to push if the remote didn't seem to be paired up. Unfortunately, the print and images were so tiny that I could not decipher what one of the buttons actually was. I tried to find an online manual that might have larger print but couldn't even find the company's website. Randomly pushing buttons finally got the cursor to appear. However, the pointer kept jutting off at odd angles whenever I tried to move the mouse. I managed to decipher the instructions for adjusting the mouse speed but that did nothing to fix the odd angling of the cursor. Moreover, while trying to use the buttons on the mouse side, I again started getting random, unexpected results. The whole thing was a mess and I finally gave up on it all. This product is useless for me. If you are tech savvy enough, you might be able to get it working properly but I'm not going to fiddle around with it anymore myself.
text_fidelity_b: AuviPal G10 Backlit 2.4GHz Wireless Air Mouse Remote with Shortcut Keys, QWERTY Keyboard and Build-in Rechargeable Battery for Windows 10 PC Laptop Tablet Win10 Mini PC Stick HTPC

text_fidelity_a:
BOSS Audio Systems B9351WRC Double Din, Touchscreen, Bluetooth, DVD CD MP3 USB SD AM FM Car Stereo, 6.2 Inch Digital LCD Monitor, Wireless Remote, Wireless Rear License Plate Camera. CD player stopped working after 3 months (just spit out cds) and the sound stopped 2 weeks later. Thus one star. Prior to that I was happy with it, so here's my review.
***UPDATE***: While it was past the Amazon return date, it was within the OEM 1yr warranty, so I sent it back and they replaced it. I had to pay shipping to them and round trip was 2 to 3 weeks without a radio. In general I do like the unit for the money, so long as this one isn't a dud.

Installation wasn't bad. I didn't need a trim kit as the one it came with was fine. I purchased a wire harness for my Nissan Frontier and crimp connectors made the connections easy. The hardest part was wiring up the backup camera. I had to find the wire to my reverse lights in a plug in the passenger foot rest and similarly I powered the backup camera by splicing into my backup light wire. That works fine, though the picture flickers occasionally. I suspect that's the wiring/ power and not a camera issue.

Sound quality was fine while it lasted. It does cut out the first second of each song when listening to my iPhone over Bluetooth, but that was only a minor annoyance. The touch screen interface worked fine for me. The interface isn't super intuitive but the icons are nice and big and the screen sensitivity was fine. It was great value for the money for the 3 months that it worked.
text_fidelity_b: BOSS Audio Systems B9351WRC Double Din, Touchscreen, Bluetooth, DVD CD MP3 USB SD AM FM Car Stereo, 6.2 Inch Digital LCD Monitor, Wireless Remote, Wireless Rear License Plate Camera.

SOSUN Video Camera Camcorder HD 1080P 24.0MP 3.0 Inch LCD 270 Degrees Rotatable Screen 16X Digital Zoom Camera Recorder and 2 Batteries(301S-Plus), 301AM I haven't bothered with a video camera in many years - using an excellent cell phone camera is just so much easier and convienent. That is still the case when I decide between using this camera vs my LG V40 phone for quick video of the dogs and horses. However, I did take the video camera with me to Big Bend National Park last week and tried it out there.

There are two rechargeable batteries and they offer far more use time than I expected. Swapping them out is pretty simple once you figure out where they go. The instructions are skimpy, but things are reasonably logical. The little carrying case is padded and the entire camera and case fits perfectly in a side pocket of a small hiking pack.

Actual use is straightforward. The camera fits in your palm and the record, photo and zoom buttons are designed to be pressed with just a thumb. I do like the view screen - it rotates and lets you really see what you're filming. For wide, expansive vistas like West Texas offers, this camera is fine and captures the vast distance of the landscape. However, close up details are fuzzy - I sincerely doubt this is true 1080p quality simply because the video shot from my phone is sharper and prettier. This is essentially a fine, basic little video camera that won't break a budget if it's lost or stolen.
text_fidelity_b: SOSUN Video Camera Camcorder HD 1080P 24.0MP 3.0 Inch LCD 270 Degrees Rotatable Screen 16X Digital Zoom Camera Recorder and 2 Batteries(301S-Plus), 301AM

I wanted an e-ink reader, so I got this when it was offered to me as a discount.

In general, it's okay. I do not read in the dark and try not to use the backlight, but without the backlight the text is pretty dark. I have to use a bold font to read properly. The touch screen is very uncooperative compared with the tablet. You have to poke and poke to get things to work, even turning the pages. I wish there was a volume control on this one which you could use to turn pages instead. It's also not very intuitive where everything is. For instance, once I finish a book and wish to go back to the front to collect information for a review--the copyright date, for instance, or the name of a character--I have to mess around trying to get back to the first page.

I gave it four stars because the battery life is incredible and it doesn't bother my eyes as much, but for the touch screen it might get closer to three stars.

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I bought this to take on a trip. I am traveling very lightly, and I do not like waiting around. I have a smartphone, but it's getting harder for me to read on it. I have an iPad Air, but even that can be a little big on a cramped plane ride.

Plus, I sold my other seven inch tablets (a Galaxy and a MeMo), and I miss them. They're the perfect size for reading. This tablet is so much nicer than what I would have been willing to deal with for fifty bucks. However, there are a couple of issues that keep this from being a five star device, even at this price.

The first is that using an sd card to hold content is no easier than it is with the older tech media players I have spent a fair amount of time trying to figure out. If you can download it to your computer, you can put it on the card and then load the card into the Kindle, but the Kindle doesn't treat the card like a drive that you can save to. A firmware update could fix this.

The second is the weight. I'm actually not sure how I feel about this one. It's definitely heavier than I expected. But it feels solid. So, maybe I like it?

We got another one listed at $40 and besides for the branding, it seems to be the same binocular with slight molding differences. The tech is the same. Don't bother spending a little more unless you really want to upgrade and get one with zoom function. All these economy versions do not have zoom. And if you're new to binoculars, there is a learning curve, but this is how you focus:

1. Set the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial to ZERO and set sight on a distant subject. I'm not sure what zero means since there are no numbers, but there are arrows, so I presume it's when the arrows line up.

2. Cover the RIGHT FRONT lens with your hand, and rotate the FOCUSING WHEEL (the middle wheel), until the image is sharp. Keep both eyes open while you make this adjustment.

3. Now cover the LEFT FRONT lens and rotate the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial until the image is sharp. So here, you're not touching the focusing wheel, you're adjusting the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial.
text_fidelity_b: 12x42 Binoculars for Adults - HD Low Light Night Vision - Compact Lightweight (1.05lb) - Powerful BAK4 Prism FMC Lens - Waterproof Binoculars for Bird Watching, Hunting, Sports -Phone Adapter Included

It is portable enough to lug over to your buddy's house for play dates, but it is too bulky and heavy to carry to work everyday. Construction is very good with an aggressive-looking aluminum case to match the aggressive-sounding "Legion" product name. Mechanical keyboard has decent (but not the best) travel and the large keys are backlit so you can easily play your games in the dark. Dolby Atmos audio works well for games, but is kind of thin for music or movies unless you hook it up to external speakers. This Y720 version has a 1080p IPS display, which is OK but not as bright or contrasty as some other laptops I have used. There is also a more expensive 4K display available, but I have not tried that.

Core i7 CPU with 16GB of RAm gives you really great performance. This machine is easily powerful enough for any games I tried on it. Even though performance is throttled somewhat when run off the battery, battery life is still less than 2 hours under heavy use (maybe 6 hours with light use).

For the money, it is hard to go wrong with these Lenovo Legions. If you don't want to spend more than $1000, the cheaper Legion Y520 is almost as good for most types of games and costs $300 less.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo Legion Y720 Gaming Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, Intel Core i7-7700HQ Processor, 16GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, GeForce GTX 1060-6GB, Windows 10 Signature Image - 80VR0078US

GreatCall 5Star Urgent Response Medical Alert Device (Silver) My neighbor Mariam and I are in our mid-sixties. Her husband recommended this device so that we could get help during long walks just in case Mariam, who has a heart condition, begins to feel bad. We have great Verizon coverage in our area, and she has been very pleased with her tests of the device.

I didn't have any problems during the activation of my device: I thought that the steps were explained clearly by the Customer Service representative, who talked with me clearly and politely during our approximately 20-minute telephone call.

I have not yet retired and like the fact that this device can travel with me to work and back.

The only problem that I encountered was that initially I could not get the device to turn off. Consequently, I really couldn't figure-out whether or not it was "on" because I didn't know how to tell the difference between off and on. After several days, the "off/on" button worked properly, and I've learned that a voice speaks when it powers off and on in a way that is similar to the procedure that a cell phone uses when it powers on and off.

Because of the problem above, the cell phone was actually "on" for several days. I didn't recharge it during that time. The unit has a small "ready" light that blinks to show that the device is operating properly. The device continued blinking all week, and I am re-charging the device now and hoping to restore the full battery charge, indicated by a steady green light on the battery indicator.

It couldn't be simpler. I understand that a cell phone can be used to call 911, as well; however, it takes awhile for my cell phone to power up. It's not always easy to use. This device is simple and, hopefully, works as well as promised.

I am pleased with the battery life and so far am pleased with everything. Hope it isn't needed but am glad to have it.

D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D) This will tell you if a battery is good or bad. However since it has no internal power source, it uses the power of the battery you are testing to give you a reading. This requires a power drain on the battery you are testing, which will ALWAYS give you inaccurate results. If you take a very small battery, such as a 1.5 V watch battery that is 1/3 depleted, this may be as mush as 30% off on the low side. Example, I checked a 1.5 V watch batty and this showed 1.0 V. Using a high end, self powered volt meter, the battery shoed 1.4V. That is a huge difference.

So again, it will show you a dead battery, but so will dropping a battery on end on a hard surface, If it bounces its dead, if it thuds and does not bounce, its good. Work on all AA, AAA, C, D. batteries.
text_fidelity_b: D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D)

MUSICOZY Sleep Headphones Wireless Bluetooth 5.2 Sports Headband Headphones Earbuds Earphones with HD Stereo Speakers Unique Cool Gadgets for Running Workout Jogging Yoga Insomnia Slept two nights with these headphones in their stock configuration and decided I could create something far superior.
For several years I’ve owned and extensively used a pair of the original wired SleepPhones. They are extremely comfortable. The drivers are only 2-3mm thick and sandwiched between two layers of felt. The fleece headband stayed in place without feeling constrictive. It was also easy to wash - open the hook and loop closure on the back, pulled out the speakers and wires, wash, dry, re-install.
By contrast, MusiCozy uses thicker drivers (granted, the frequency response is better than the SleepPhone drivers) then adds a rubber cover, then covers that with a thin jersey fabric. The headband was painfully tight, and I don’t have a big head (22.5”). After the first night, I stretched the headband over a small throw pillow for a day and that helped a bit. But the second night, the thick drivers hurt my ears so bad I took the whole thing off. I mostly sleep on my side and stomach. It’s also tricky to charge because the port is only accessible if you line up the slit in the jersey fabric just right. Some simple product testing would have identified these issues. But for $20, I couldn’t be happier….. why?
SleepPhoness wants $100 for their bluetooth units. I’m sure they are top-notch but I didn’t want to spend that much. Here’s my solutions: The entire MuziCozy headband was disassembled….all two components. The bluetooth receiver / battery compartment and speakers come out easily enough. The fake ‘control panel’ on the front isn’t needed. The speakers have a rubber cover that is not needed. Once that is removed, the speakers are only 3-4mm thick, which is good. I disassembled the wired SleepPhones as well. The felt driver covers were re-used with the MuziCozy drivers, then the whole thing was re-installed into the SleepPhone headband.
This is the best setup - the headband is comfortable, I can still use it to cover my eyes, the sound quality is improved, and the MuziCozy charge port is easier to access thanks to the large velcro opening on the back of the headband.
My girlfriend, by contrast, likes absolute silence while sleeping so she uses the MuziCozy headband to make sure her earplugs don’t fall out and to cover her eyes.
So the entire unit has gone to good use, just not in the way it was delivered. I’m happy with the results but the original product need some redesign.
text_fidelity_b: MUSICOZY Sleep Headphones Wireless Bluetooth 5.2 Sports Headband Headphones Earbuds Earphones with HD Stereo Speakers Unique Cool Gadgets for Running Workout Jogging Yoga Insomnia

Amazon Basics On-Ear Headphones I use headphones very frequently under a number of different environments including noisy computer labs, airplanes, quiet rooms and more. I am particularly familiar with noise canceling phones but I do have a some non-ANC phones that I use for listening to music in quiet environments. This pair of Amazon Basics headphones is my least expensive pair but it actually compares reasonably well against some more expensive phones.

First, the Basics headphones are very lightweight on-ear phones. They are slightly tight though not so tight to cause discomfort. What they do cause for me is a bit of warmth on the ears, something that I have not experienced very often when using headphones. It’s a minor aggravation, not a show-stopper by any means.

The most important feature of any headphones is the sound profile. I like electronic music which has a wide range of sound frequency - abundant highs, full midrange and quite a bit of bass. When listening to tracks with these phones, the first thing that I could not help but notice is that they overdrive the bass a little much, but this seems to be more the norm with headphones anymore. The highs sound just about right - not exceptionally sharp but not muted either. The midrange, though, is off and reminds me of listening to music in a tunnel. It isn’t terrible, but it’s noticeable. From what I can tell, the bass is so overdriven that it partially flattens the midrange.

I compared these headphones to a pair of Munitio PRO40 phones, a much more expensive set ($350 full retail) of phones that I use for studio work. Yes, the Munitio phones outperformed the Basics phones, but the difference did not match the $300 price difference. Other than the midrange, the Basics phones compared very well on the sound spectrum. That’s more than I could have asked for at $15.

If this was an expensive set of phones I would be very upset. However, this is a VERY inexpensive set and for the price range sounds much better than average.

Construction-wise this set of phones feels well-made. They won’t hold up to abuse, but with proper care they should last a long time. They even come with a cloth carry bag with offers little more than scratch protection but it’s a nice touch.

Considering how inexpensive these headphones are, I am hard-pressed to criticize. In their price range they are well above average in terms of sound and construction. If you are looking for a lightweight and inexpensive set of headphones and you do not need the very best in sound this is an outstanding value.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics On-Ear Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography I am best described as a skilled amateur when it comes to photography and I am always looking for ways to get better and to build my knowledge and ability. I am not a professional by any means, but I know a lot more than the average selfie-taker. I have wanted a ring light for a little while and I was delighted to have the chance to get to use this one. It does work, in the right circumstances, but it is definitely aimed at the base consumer market and is priced accordingly.

Thought it can be used as part of a professional set-up, it is designed and marketed as a consumer-grade unit. There are a number of obvious design decisions that make this more than just a little apparent. The tripod is good, but the mounts are designed for smartphones and will not work for DSLR cameras, mirrorless cameras or video cameras. That’s ok, as it is clearly marketed that way. The unit uses a USB power source which is an important point – the light itself isn’t especially bright like one that uses a normal AC power source. To be effective, the light needs to be fairly close to the subject. If a dim directional light is needed, a regular desk lamp is more than adequate in most cases. The upshot is that using USB power makes it much more portable for travel (more on that in a moment).

The remote allows for making a few adjustments to the light itself. There are three color modes and ten brightness modes, all of which can be (rather, must be) set through the remote. The adjustments are sufficient for this grade of light, though I would have found more colors and a more smooth graduation in brightness to be more useful. That’s more of a nitpick than a criticism considering the price point.

Build-wise, this unit is acceptable. It should hold up well enough in the studio or home office. What is lacking is a carry case to protect it when travelling. Considering the target audience (social media producers), this is an oversight that I think is important. To transport this light, it should be well secured and the only recourse as sold is to put it back in the original box, and that’s just unwieldy. Plan accordingly if you choose to transport this light.

This is an adequate unit for its target audience but will leave the aspiring professional underwhelmed. If you are looking for something that will work sufficiently for making posts to social media this is a reasonable unit; if you need a serious ring light for photography, consider other options. The main problem with this light is the fact that it is designed for portability but comes with no carrying case; keep this in mind.
text_fidelity_b: B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging I have a Nuvi 360. It came with a suction cup windshield mount. It also came with a steel disk with double sticky adhesive on the back. I was supposed to mount this disk somewhere on my dashboard, then use the suction cup to attach the mount. I didn't want to use the suction mount directly onto the windshield because 1) it telegraphs the presence of an expensive GPS unit, 2) it's illegal in California to attach anything to the windshield and 3) I don't think the suction cup would last very long.

Then there's the disk with the very permanent double sticky tape. The problem with almost all cars these days is there really isn't anywhere to attach the disk discreetly. Every square inch is taken with existing stuff. And who wants an ugly disk glued to the dash anyway? And what if I want to use the GPS in other vehicles? More disks?

So I settled on this "beanbag" mount with the ball mount arm.

Unfortunately, before the beanbag friction mount arrived, I was flexing the arm in the suction cup mount and noticed the suction cup's mounting bracket had already broken. I had never even attached it to anything! The mount is beautifully engineered and built...except for one area where the arm's hinge pin attaches to the suction cup's plastic hinge loops. The loops are too thin and fragile. The loops cracked and broke with hardly any hinging at all.

So now I have a quite useless suction mount but a very functional ball arm. What to do?

I drove the hinge pin out of the ball arm. Then I took two small 1" x 1" steel angle brackets and attached them to the ball arm with a 2" long, 8-32 threaded machine screw and an 8-32 wingnut. This created two "feet" for the ball arm. Then I epoxied the two bracket "feet" to the fabric (upper) side of an old 1/4" thick mousepad. Ta da. A friction pad for pennies with a ball arm attached.

Works great. Cost was virtually nothing. Doesn't slide on either of the two dashboards I've tried it on. The mousepad is flexible and conforms easily to the curving shape of the various dashboards. It doesn't weigh much but the thick mousepad has enough heft to plant the getup nicely. The grippy rubber side of the mousepad adheres nicely to the dash. Yet I can pull it down to the floor quickly and reposition it easily.

I wish I'd thought of this BEFORE I ordered this "official" friction mount to the tune of a couple of twenties.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging

Overall this is a $10 case marked up cause they can. I mean we have expensive headphones so why not charge us more? We have already proven we will pay.

Skip this thing. Mine is going back. If you want something to protect them in a backpack then still look elsewhere. You can get something equal to this for less.

Thanks for your time.

text_fidelity_a:
Acer G236HL Bbd 23-Inch Screen LED-Lit Monitor I would love to give a higher rating, but I think "1 star" is the only way to summarize my experience with this product.

Amazon shipped quickly (as usual). I tried to put it together the night it arrived. It comes in 3 pieces: base, arm, and monitor. The only instructions were a simple diagram showing how they roughly fit together. The base and arm fit together nicely, but the arm would not snap into the monitor. I could see how it was designed to snap together, but the metal part was too large to fit into the space on the back of the monitor. I could technically place the monitor on top of the arm+base, but it was very loose and could easily fall over if bumped slightly.

I called Acer tech support, hoping there was some trick I couldn't figure out. There wasn't. After suggesting that I push harder (I had already pushed hard enough that I was worried about breaking the monitor), go back to the store for assistance (huh?), and return the entire monitor, they agreed to send a replacement part.

1.5 weeks later, I called back asking for a status update on the part. I was informed that the part hadn't been ordered (huh?) and that I could call back the next day to have it ordered (wtf?). The rep agreed that this was a less-than-wonderful customer experience, but explained that there was nothing she could do (she wasn't allowed to place the replacement part order).

At that point, I gave up and started the return process with Amazon (which, btw, is always awesome when I have to do it).

So, I guess this is mainly a review of Acer QA and customer service, both of which completely failed for me. Considering the other reviews, I'm hoping that my experience is rare, but I'll be trying a different brand for my next monitor.
text_fidelity_b: Acer G236HL Bbd 23-Inch Screen LED-Lit Monitor

text_fidelity_a:
PIONEER Truly Wireless in-Ear Headphones, Black, SE-C8TW(B) If you're an iphone user, you're probably wondering whether to buy these Pioneer wireless headphones or the Apple version. The Pioneer price is about 1/3 cheaper than Apple. The Pioneer earbuds fit in your ear, so you get much better sound and much better sound isolation. These are nowhere near as detailed or loud as similarly priced wired headphones, but that's true of all wireless Bluetooth earbuds. I will say the connection is stable and not noisy, so these are better than most cheap Bluetooth earbuds. There is some bass, but don't work well for bass-heavy music. Maximum volume is just OK. Battery life is only about 3 hours per charge (compared to 5 hours for Apple), then you have to put the earbuds back in the case for a 1 hour charge. 3 hours may be enough for you; you have to decide, but 5 hours is certainly going to be more interesting to most people. The charging case is much larger than the Apple charging case. The case is 3.3 inches long and 2.2 inches wide. These case is to big to fit comfortably in my pants pocket, so I would only carry it with me in a backpack or purse.

Usage is pretty simple. They paired easily with my phone as a normal Bluetooth device. The buttons on the headphones are easy to use. They are comfortable in my ears. They are secure enough so far, never feeling like they are going to fall out. They are not noticeably heavy like some earbuds can be. When in my ears, they are much less ugly than the Apple earbuds.

I would give these 5 stars for the price and performance if the sound and battery life were better. Frankly, I've tried a few different totally wireless earbuds and been less than impressed by all of them. Bluetooth headphones that have a wire connecting the two pieces can be had for much lower prices and have much better sound quality and much better battery life. Removing the wire just doesn't seem worth the downsides to me.
text_fidelity_b: PIONEER Truly Wireless in-Ear Headphones, Black, SE-C8TW(B)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Wireless Desktop MK 300 I love my laptop; it's freed me to work in any room in the house and for that alone I'd nominate it for the greatest invention of the century. ButI don't much like the keyboard and I flat-out hate the touch pad, so I've been wanting a free-standing mouse for a while now. Along came the Logitech desktop bundle and suddenly I've got the sort of flexibility I'd been craving. They aren't kidding when they say it's ready to work right out of the box. I could do all the most basic functions without ever programming a thing. Once I installed the software, I got a lot more control. I was able to program the mouse buttons to give me single, double and right click functions as well as scrolling, the most common functions for my work. The keyboard functions include an easy application switcher, a button which boots up the default email program, and one which I've programmed to open my browser. Another key opens the control panel, and a fifth I've programmed to bring up my documents window -- a huge time-saver for a writer. There's also a key to bring up the calculator. Function keys are similarly programmable, and with the amount of choice I have I could automate all of my most common tasks and still have keys left over. There are also control keys for audio functions, and all the standard keys including a keypad which was sorely missed in my laptop. There's even a key to check battery status on both mouse and keyboard.

One of the things I liked most about the keyboard is that it can apparently be secured against keystroke monitors. Not that I have a lot of concern about that particular issue with my set-up, but people who are working in unsecured office space might well appreciate that feature.

The keys have a good, solid feel to them, and are surprisingly quiet for a stand-alone keyboard. The mouse works beautifully on a bare desk, and has a good hand feel.

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black) I made absolutely sure everything was closed before putting it into water, not that one could have much faith in the mechanisms keeping it closed, as they are easy to accidentally open. I put it in the water gently, and only a foot or so, to film some stingrays and fish; this recording went fine. Later that day, I wanted to photograph a tiny little crab. I took one picture from above the water, and one from below. I noticed this time, when I put the camera underwater, that bubbles started to come out the top. I immediately took it out and noticed the screen starting to fog up with condensation and moisture, the first very bad sign. I double checked everything was still closed, and it was. No part of it had been opened. I put it back in, hoping for the best. After coming back to the sand (never having done more than a few feet underwater), I tried to turn it on to get some video. It would not turn on. I checked again, and nothing appeared to be open. I then dried the exterior and opened it, only to discover there was water on the inside. I immediately removed the SD card, in hopes of salvaging it, but the camera was (is) completely dead.

Two days later, there is corrosion forming on the inside from the water, but at least I salvaged the content on the SD card. The results? Video quality is fine above and below water. Photo quality is a mess. Absolutely the worst pics imaginable.
I am so glad I didn't have to pay for this product; I would have been furious it didn't even last a day in the ocean.

I expected more, since I had previously purchased a "Kodak EasyShare Sport C123 12 MP Waterproof Digital Camera", which has been great! That product never failed after much abuse and takes decent picture and video. I'm not sure what happened here, but buyer beware! Try the EasyShare Sport instead.

I'll post some pictures and, if it lets me, some video too. I hope you all find this helpful!

UPDATE: I can't post video (sorry)
Also, I looked at some other reviews that mentioned water getting in while at the pool or in other non-salinated water. Bear in mind that many electronics can survive water immersion if it is fresh water (as opposed to salt water). Many of these reviewers gave the camera more than one star because it was able to work again, but bear in mind this will NOT hold true it Salt water enters the device. Please consider this.
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter I wanted to hear and see Skype on our Sony XBR7 HDMI-only capable 1080p TV, fed from a Lenovo X220 convertable laptop/tablet running System 7 64 bit Ultimate through the DisplayPort. I also wanted to watch some YouTube videos playing from Firefox and hear their audio on my big living room audio system. No such luck.

When first plugged in, I remember briefly seeing the TV via this DisplayPort adapter in the audio device list, but the next time, the TV disappeared and is nowhere to be found. Not in the audio control panel, anyway. It's just gone.

I first chalked this up to the Thinkpad weirdness, as its internal audio card/mic doesn't work with Skype either. If I plug in an external Logitech webcam, it works seamlessly. Internal camera/mic, nothing.

Sony audio problems aside, the video looks great on the big screen, though it overscans a bit and cuts off part of the menu bar at the bottom.

One reviewer said he could see his TV in the list of audio devices and was able to configure its audio to satisfaction. My Sony TV does not show in the Lenovo audio devices list, though it does show as a generic PnP monitor.

I plugged the HDMI cable into a tiny 7" video monitor and whatdayaknow, the audio came through and the device showed up as an audio device. Then I plugged it into a 20" Vizio and sure enough, it works fine too. Same with a Samsung LCD. Three monitors out of four work. The Sony is the only one that doesn't. Hmmmm.

Sooooo, I'm guessing there's something about Sony's DRM or some other HDMI protocol blocking the computer from seeing the TV. I set all the TVs for internal speakers. Routing audio to an external amp is another variable in the equation.

Nothing wrong with the adapter that I can tell, it simply doesn't see certain Sony TV's.
text_fidelity_b: Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter

text_fidelity_a:
My Zone Wireless Headphones I got these headphones because I tend to put the TV on much louder than is comfortable for my husband, and the price was quite affordable. (That is to say, cheap.) Unfortunately, the saying, "You get what you pay for," applies in spades to my experience with this product.

I could not get the headphones hooked up by myself, and my husband, who is an IT guy, had to fiddle with them on and off over several days. He finally had to buy an [[ASIN:B000068O51 adapter]] to get it to work with our TiVo and TV combination, but while he could use the earphones once hooked up with little static, this was not the case for me. I had lots of static problems.

Here are the instructions we figured out to make it work with a TiVo, as well as it can be made to work once it is hooked up:

1. Pick up the headphones and the remotes for the TV and TiVo.
2. Stand directly in front of the TV.
3. Turn on the transmitter for the headphones.
4. Turn on the remote headphones by spinning the volume control dial on one side of the headphones. You might hear or feel a click when you spin the dial. A red light on the headphones will come on when they are turned on.
5. Press the Reset button on the headphones.
6. Put your finger on the Scan button on the remote headphones so you will know where it is.
7. Put the headphones on.
8. Press the Scan button.
9. You should now hear the sound of the TV through the headphones.
10. If you do not hear the TV, press Scan again until you hear the TV through the headphones.
11. You control the volume in the headphones with the volume dial on the side of the headphones.
12. You should turn the TV volume all the way down (or very low) using the TV remote since the TV remote does not control the volume of the headphones.

I rate this product as follows:

Ease of installation: 1 star
Ease of Use: 4 stars
Effectiveness of Product: 4 stars for IT husband, 2 stars for me, average 3 stars
Overall rating: 2.7 rounded to 3 stars
text_fidelity_b: My Zone Wireless Headphones

iPad Pro 10.5 Case with Wireless Keyboard, Janvvoo Ultra-Thin Lightweight Bluetooth Keyboard with Magnetically Intelligent Switch and Multi-Angle Stand for Apple iPad Pro 10.5 inch Tablet I have owned this shredder for over six years, and it has endured some heavy use. It is the second home-shredder I've owned, and it is much the better of the two. It is heavy enough that it doesn't tip over, but not so heavy it can't be hauled from room to room by someone moderately strong. The front compartment holding the shredded paper is easily removed--in an identical fashion to our dehumidifier's bucket. You pull on it and the bucket comes out with a forward motion. The sound the shredder makes when in action is loud, as one would expect, but not so loud that you need protective ear plugs, such as for when you are near a kitchen blender, blow dryer, leaf blower or lawn mower.

The main thing to be careful about is to not get impatient and overload the shredder blades. Yes, you can use the backup function to try and back out paper you have overloaded it with, but it is a pain. Secondly, be sure and feed paper in straight. If you feed it in crooked, that, too, is a prescription for a jam.

When I am shredding, I lay down either a bed sheet or a tarp and set the shredder in the middle of it. This helps me corral the scraps of shredded paper flying around when I empty the bucket into a trash bag. Another option is to shred in your garage or basement, if you have such spaces, and use a [[ASIN:B00005AXI1 Shop-Vac]] to clean up afterwards. If you do it inside your house, plan on having to use a regular vacuum to clean up after each use, because a mess is almost unavoidable no matter how careful you are since this shredder is turning private papers into confetti. That's great for the shredder's intended purpose, but it does have a tendency to give whatever room you are using a strong resemblance to Times Square on New Year's Eve.
text_fidelity_b: iPad Pro 10.5 Case with Wireless Keyboard, Janvvoo Ultra-Thin Lightweight Bluetooth Keyboard with Magnetically Intelligent Switch and Multi-Angle Stand for Apple iPad Pro 10.5 inch Tablet

Canon EF-S 55-250mm F4-5.6 IS STM Lens with UV Protection Filter - 58 mm I purchased this lens on Amazon offered by a gray market vendor for $140 (new!). Gray Market means there is no USA Warranty. I haven't tried to see if it is eligible, but I assume it would not be. As of this writing (10/12/2014), that vendor, CD Supply, is still offering the lens - though now for $170. Still an incredible deal for this lens which came new in the standard Canon box with manual etc. (If it isn't warranteed - I can buy another and still be about the price of just one at regular price).

The lens itself: I was pleasantly surprised. I could have purchased it in my kit with the 70D camera, but wasn't really interested. For $140 - what the heck. The photos are sharper than from the kit 18-135mm STM IS lens in my opinion (and that's a pretty decent lens as kit lenses go). It is very small and light weight for a pretty long lens - especially on a crop sensor.
BONUS: Macro. It actually can get pretty decent magnification. Something like 1/4:1 from a pretty good distance at 250mm.
Plus it works great with extension tubes. I've used it with 12mm and 26mm (not together) and it worked great. Even autofocus - though I wouldn't recommend that for Macro.

Negatives (though - again - if you get it for cheap, these are quibbles):
- No lens hood provided. Buy a knock off on Amazon for $13
- Not a super bright lens. You're going to need some decent sunlight or a good flash with this. It ramps up to f/5 minimum pretty quick and f/5.6 not too long after that. Only the widest shots will get F/4.
- Pretty cheaply built (but it's a cheap lens!)

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate We have several networked devices in our house and also several individualized networks configured. Not all of the networks can be seen by all devices so I looked to this Belkin USB WiFi adapter to allow one of the older computer systems to access the most reliable network in the house - a 5GHz network that only one or two of the systems can see.

Installation was a snap. I popped in the CD, told it to install the drivers and we were off to the races. The particular target system was a 32-bit Windows Vista laptop. After just a couple of minutes the driver was completely installed and when I plugged in the USB adapter is was picked up immediately. I could see the desired network as well as several other networks in the neighborhood that were previously invisible to the computer. I shut off the built-in adapter, connected to the 5GHz network and went to the net.

So far, the connection has been very stable and speeds have been excellent. The router to which it is connected is a TP-Link router and so far we have seen no issues between the two devices. I have not had this adapter very long so it is still early to say it’s completely stable but all indicators up to this point have been very favorable.

Several other reviewers have mentioned that this adapter does not work with Linux. This is true - there are no drivers available for this adapter other than for Windows XP/Vista/7/8. If you need an adapter that will allow you to connect a Linux or Mac system to a wireless network, this is not the device you need right now.

So far I can’t find too much about which to complain concerning this router. It seems to be stable and reliable on the system to which it is attached here. I am satisfied with it and based on my experience with it can recommend it - if you’re sticking with Windows.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab (7-inch, 16GB, Wi-Fi) I really liked this 7" Tab (GT-P1010) at first. It's most useful function is web surfing.

Now, after several months of use, it's SLOOOOOOOW to load and update pages and locks up occasionally for no particular reason. I've uninstalled every unnecessary app but whether using the default Browser or Dolphin, it's more frustrating than useful.

It's also inaccurate for when inputting via keyboard. Oftentimes the keyboard adds wild characters all by itself.

Forget firmware updates. You are stuck with whatever it came with. And if you think Samsung will be any help, think again. I put "GT-P1010" in Samsung's product support page and got "no results."

I have to say Apple's major firmware updates work a whole lot better. First, because they happen at all and second, because they are seamless and reliable. Android is buggy and needs fixing on this Samsung Tablet. Samsung's "answer" is to buy a new tablet.

The device has two cameras and would be ideal for video chatting, but won't work with Skype. Apparently it needs the next version of Android. (See above concerning that impossibility.) But who knows if the next-up model will work either?

These things all want to be Apple but simply fall short.

One nice thing is that most Flash content is supported when web surfing. Apple is way lacking here. I used an iPad 1 for some time and it's pretty frustrating that it simply ignores so much content.

Bottom line is I won't buy another wannabe Samsung device like this that lacks firmware updates. (I did the same thing looking for the perfect mp3 player: everyone tried to sell the "iPod killer" and I spent more money trying to avoid the iPod. Then I bought an iPod3 and later an iPhone4 and understood how excellent their engineering and software and OS are and how with OS updates the devices continually get better even after you make the purchase.) They are too expensive to throw away and Samsung can't or won't fix the bugs. Thus you are stuck with an expensive, buggy toy that's frustrating to use. No thank you.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab (7-inch, 16GB, Wi-Fi)

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Compared to a similar camera made by Belkin, setting up the D-Link was kind of a pain. Not as much of a pain as setting up a Foscam F18918W - where you get directed to a third party domain name provider and get to learn the joys of port forwarding - but a relative hassle.

For the Belkin, I opened the box, plugged into my router, ran a set up program that took less than five minutes, downloaded an app, and I was up and running. While this is a very similar product in both look and function, it took over an hour - and two ethernet cables - to set it up. There is no Mac software on the installation cd. The box states that a Windows pc is required, but the website has a Mac download available. You have to scroll through the product photos, which aren't in alphanumeric order. Just keep looking until you find the DCS-930L - AFTER the 931L and the 932L and the 934L. Have faith. Keep going. It's there.

Once you get the program installed, it takes very little time to *find* the camera and teach it to log into your wireless network. And then you are back to the website to set up your account and view your camera. Except you are on a Mac, and the viewer requires you to install the Java Runtime Environment. JRE is a big old security vulnerability on Macs. So much so that Apple advises against using it. Mavericks lets you turn it on case by case - and, by default, it will ask you every time before running it. If you are on an OS below Mavericks, check the googles for setting your preferences so that you're not running JRE all the time.

Okay, so now you've got JRE going, and the first thing the program tells you is that you have to update your firmware AND you need to have the camera AND your computer ethernet-jacked right into your router. LOLWUT? I'm lucky. I am on a laptop, and I have an extra ethernet cable and an empty port. So, I did that, and there I was, up and running, about an hour, hour and a half, thereabouts, after I started.

Image quality is pretty good - not great. Audio is okay. The settings are very customizable. But the wifi receiver is very weak, and that limits the usefulness of this product.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Next issue is that it doesn't come with DVD playing software. Seriously? Why did I buy a computer with a DVD player in it? Asus support informs me that I should buy a third party DVD playing app as Microsoft won't let them include it. Really. I ended up researching and finding VLC player but come on. My Toshiba windows 10 laptop came with DVD playing software and it doesn't even HAVE a dvd drive!

Finally, I'm very used to having the function keys be utility keys. Brightness, volume, etc. And I like it that way. I don't use the F functions often (F11 is about the only one) and prefer to use the fn key for them when I do. Asus is set up to do the opposite. Most other manufacturers give you a way to reverse that behavior. EIther a fn lock key or a bios setting or something. Not Asus. Nope, you're stuck with it the way they like it.

Unfortunately I'm stuck with this laptop since Amazon has a lousy return policy on computers. Maybe some 13 year old will think it's cool and want to buy it. I hope so.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ROG GL552VW-DH74 15-Inch Gaming Laptop, Discrete GPU GeForce GTX 960M 4GB VRAM, 16GB DDR4, 1TB, 128GB SSD (ROG Metallic)

EagleTec HUB3639 USB 2.0, 4 Port Hub, Ultra Slim Compact USB Hub for Laptop PC Computer (Black) Since my MacBook Air has only 2 USB ports, and I have a bunch of external devices and gizmos that need to talk to the Mac via USB, I set out looking for something that would allow me to attach multiple USB-connectable devices at the same time. One of the 2 MacBook Air USB ports is dedicated to my 1TB external hard drive, but I also have a wireless mouse, a 25-key midi keyboard that I use for composing music, and a few other things that I may not use every day, but that I want to be able to use without having to disconnect my mouse.

Saw this, read the reviews, and decided to give it a try. So far, we've been working together comfortably for just over a week with no hiccups or mishaps. I like the small size -- it's small and relatively "flat," so it stays tucked just behind my laptop on my desk without occupying too much real estate. I like that.

I have the wireless mouse "receiver" plugged into the end, my midi keyboard plugged into the first of the 3 slots on the side, and I can add anything else (iPhone for syncing, etc.) in one of the other two slots. This summer, I'll be using it with a USB-driven personal fan when the weather warms up (no air conditioning here in the Pacific NW). I did test all 4 ports, and they are all working just fine.

Very happy with it so far. If I start noticing any issues, I'll update this review.

The Heysliy Light Box Photography lightbox is just that and nothing more. Designed to be portable, the box can be folded flat and comes with a carrying bag that nicely stores everything in the kit.

Unfortunately, it's the execution of the thing that is to be desired. The box is cut from a sheet of translucent plastic then folded to form a box. The flaps are joined by a barely-tight-enough screw cap that can be easily lost because it is not actually part of the box. The plastic itself is stuff, but has an elastic memory, which means that it wants to fold back to its storage position, weakening the sides of the box unless the flaps are folded outward first. Overall, the structure is quite flimsy and can be tricky to set up.

The Heysliy lightbox comes with four backdrops made of that paper-like material that is used by some reuseable grocery bags. The colors are black, white, green, and red. The backdrop is hung by a hole cut into the material and a tab that's cut into the plastic box. Any hard tug will rip that backdrop so be careful.

So the conclusion is that the box is annoying to set up and with the LED's mounted on the inside of the box, reflections will be a big issue with this box as can be seen in my pictures (nintendo switch pictured for size reference).
text_fidelity_b: Heysliy Product Photography Light Box 16x16 Inch,Adjustable Bright Photo Box with Lights,Portable Photo Studio Light Box

Blink XT Home Security Camera System - 5 Camera Kit - 1st Gen I had an Arlo set-up, and while I really liked it, I was constantly changing batteries. (Busy street).
I saw these read some good reviews and liked the battery life.
Plus they take regular AA batteries. Easy to install. But the hangers are not very flexible, you are limited in how you are able to position the camera. For example, I have one camera up on the side of my carport, and I need for it to tilt down and to the left. With the provided hanger, that is not possible. I will make an adapter for this, but after th ease of positioning of the Arlos, I am disappointed.
Set-up was a breeze, after hanging them where I wanted them, I opened the mobile app, connected them to the supplied Bridge, and Wifi. Made adjustments to various app settings and done, reading instructions, hanging and set-up in under an hour. One of the nice aspects is the zones, (you can "block" areas from motion detection on individual cameras. so Doorways or street, sidewalks, etc to fit high traffic and pedestrian areas.
The presets are nice, but for some like me who have unusual areas to cover, some time and subtle adjustments will be needed.
The storage provided for free is adequate for me.
What I am not a fan of is the delay in recording, a couple seconds, but enough time for things/people to move out of camera view.

I bought the 43" QLED Q60B. Also bought the Samsung 9200S soundbar with wireless sub, and then bought their wireless rear speakers. That part is awesome, but will be a separate review.

1- Despite checking answers and even asking the Samsung Specialist about Hands Free Alexa (ie. don't press the MIC button), the 2022 version DOES NOT have this feature, which of course, after buying it, installing it 10ft up in the corner of the bedroom, and trying to make it work.... had to call Samsung directly to troubleshoot, who said it is not available after 2021. Even Bixby, which I can't stand, is grayed out.

2- Not-so-Smart. I have had a ROKU on all my other Samsung TVs because they were older. So I became accustomed to much more variety it seems. Other than the big ones, the variety is disappointing, even in the music section.

3- I do not buy a TV outright only to have the manufacturer decide what I CAN'T remove. The first damn option in your "customizing" short cut bar, is SAMSUNG'S forced-on-you advertising slot, that cannot be moved out of the or removed, and I have no interest in it! There are a few others that can't be dropped, but can be moved.

4- Despite trying to follow the trend to smaller remotes, they missed the mark. People want quick access to things. Mute should ALWAYS have it's own button, not remembering to press and hold a specific button to mute it. Your Settings access is NOT intuitive. I trying to make it easier, you somehow over-complicated it. Some items are ambiguous (maybe it's under this one?), and I find myself searching for things and when I finally find them, the controls are often limited.

It's 2022, I just bought a quality TV from a previously adored and promoted-by-me brand, and I'm super pissed. My buddy's LG is much better, and I'm now going to add a fricking Roku to a TV that is state of the art. And for a 43" I could have gotten an off-name brand with awesome pic and Roku built in, for half the price!!!! Lesson Learned!

Boo to Samsung on this. And don't send me to your useless Facebook help page when you already dropped the ball!

I also have the Liberty 2 Upgraded version, and while those are very good, these are clearly superior.

I did use the Soundcore app to update the firmware and enable LDAC: you'll definitely want to do this before you begin using them. Also, there are other settings on the app you might find useful.

They are also very comfortable to wear for long periods (I use them at my desk while working), and even using LDAC (which uses a lot more power) the battery lasts as long as I've needed so far. The case is nice and compact, and of course charges the earbuds quickly. The only thing I would grumble about (and now I'm being very fussy) is that I have to turn the earbuds over to get them into the right position for the case.

Another note: Anker was offering a "used like new" item for a much lower price, so I decided to try them. I'm very happy I did, since they really were just like a new product, seemed unused (probably a quick return). All the earpiece bits were new, of course.

Highly recommended for excellent sound and comfort at a very affordable price (new or used).

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link Deco Whole Home Mesh WiFi System (Deco S4) – Up to 2,000 Sq.ft. Coverage, WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Gigabit Ports, 1-Pack Been using for a few months now. Initially seemed like an excellent upgrade over an inexpensive single wifi router, but I've seen enough issues that I'm not sure I'd buy again. The worst failure was when I switched from Verizon Fios coax to ethernet and tried to use this as my main router. It worked... for about a week. At first, I just had trouble connecting to corp sites, so I thought it might be my corp network. Later that day, I saw issues with personal devices. Connecting to the router web page was super sluggish and the cpu was pegged. The next day, I went back to using the verizon router as the wired backbone and only using this set for wifi---much better. But, I still see occasional flakiness. Yesterday, one of the units wouldn't connect. I brought it closer to the other units---no dice. I rebooted. I connected it to the network via an ethernet cable. Finally, I rebooted the main/router unit and things went back to normal. Every 2-4 weeks one of the units has issues. Sometimes rebooting that unit is enough. Occasionally I have to reboot the main unit. One of the extender units connects via both wifi and powerline. The other extender unit only connects via powerline (it's too far to use wifi). The powerline-only unit is the one that tends to have issues. But, that was the point of buying this system.

So, the system seems good as long as you don't mind doing a ~weekly reboot. I see about 30Mbps over the powerline-only unit---not fast, but generally reliable.

I've started using MoCA (ethernet over coax) and will likely use that as my backbone in the near future---it's faster (I've seen ~300Mbps for a local transfer over MoCA/ethernet/wifi) and seems to be more reliable than this tp-link set over powerline.

Edit: I ditched this in favor of an EdgeRouter X and Ubiquity access points and am happier now. The Deco system was okay, but far from ideal.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link Deco Whole Home Mesh WiFi System (Deco S4) – Up to 2,000 Sq.ft. Coverage, WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Gigabit Ports, 1-Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz S1 IEM Noise Isolating Earphones With Clearwavz Remote and Microphone for iPhone iPad iPod I’m really impressed with these earphones. Usually with mid-priced earphones you have to qualify the sound with the phrase “for the price.” Not with these – they put out sound that rivals earbuds I have that cost 3 to 4 times more.

The clarity is spot-on. Nice crisp treble and midrange, but not at the expense of a goodly amount of bass. Not skull-shaking bass, but clean, non-boomy bass that rounds out the sound perfectly.

The overall build quality is excellent. It does have a potentially polarizing feature: a flat cable. Personally, I really like the flat cable. The style is helpful in keeping the earbuds in place (since these are over-the-ear style buds) and helps keep cord tangles to a minimum. There’s also a small slider on the cable yoke that can be adjusted to keep them secure when wearing them while in motion. However, others who have borrowed these from me were not as enthused about the flat cable. No one hated it, but the reaction was occasionally on the lukewarm side.

Wearing comfort is another point where these excel. Lightweight, nice ear canal feel, and solid sound isolation. It comes with a variety of tips to ensure a good fit for pretty much anyone. I’d suggest trying a variety of sizes since bass response and sound isolation are affected by how well these fit in your ears.

Also included is a nicely styled case that holds the earbuds plus the accessory tips. It’s well-made, attractive and designed for actual use, with small mesh pockets to hold things in place.

The 3.5mm plug is angled to make it easy to use plus stay out of the way better than the conventional straight type plug when using it on a small mp3 player.

Try as I might, I can’t come up with a single negative about these. Built well, sounds great, and thoughtful design touches throughout. Collectively, that makes these one of the best values in earbuds I’ve run across so far, and I would highly recommend them.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz S1 IEM Noise Isolating Earphones With Clearwavz Remote and Microphone for iPhone iPad iPod

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Sense 2 Advanced Health and Fitness Smartwatch with Tools to Manage Stress and Sleep, ECG App, SpO2, 24/7 Heart Rate and GPS, Shadow Grey/Graphite, One Size (S & L Bands Included) At this point, I have had the Sense 2 for 2 days and I know at least some of my issues will likely be fixed with later software updates. First, the good. I like the form factor. The case is thin and the watch, even with the supplied band, is comfortable. Speaking of the band, as a big guy, I was overjoyed to see the inclusion of a second band that actually fit. Also, changing bands is a snap.

Overall, it seems to be relatively high quality. The battery life, so far at least has been fantastic. I am on hour 42 of wearing it after a 99% charge and it is down to 70% battery left. The screen is fairly bright and crisp. An understated advantage of the Sense 2 (and one of the reasons I switched) is that is OS and phone brand agnostic. You can use it with Apple or Android and, unlike the Galaxy Watch, there are no features locked away if you are not using the correct brand of phone.

If you are coming from a Galaxy Watch where you could customize the watch face and all sorts of other things and that is important to you, then move along. This watch will not be for you. For now, at least, there is not really much substantive you can do to individualize your user experience. That's not so great.

Also not so great is the things that are missing. There is no Google Maps at launch. Also, despite being a Google company, no support for the Google Assistant (Alexa only sadly). There is also no interface to control music on your phone if that is important to you. I found it mildly annoying, but not a deal breaker. In addition, some people will be turned off by the fact that there are features that require a Fitbit paid subscription to get, even though you get six months for free.

The real reason I bought this watch was the ECG function. I have had A Fib for a couple of years and used to use (and still do) a Kardia XL to check my rhythm. The Galaxy Watch 4 was nice because it did a reasonable single lead reading and it meant not having to carry another gizmo with me. You simply held still and put a finger on each of the side buttons. Unfortunately, when I switched from a Galaxy phone to a Pixel, I lost the ability to do an ECG.

On the Sense 2, the ECG has not been impressive. First, I have big hands and contorting my right one to get my thumb and forefinger on the corner of the glass has been a challenge at time. It often takes several tries to get it right. Second, despite confirming on both my Kardia and my Galaxy Watch, the Sense 2 will never indicate that I am in A Fib. Apparently, if your pulse goes above 120 (which mine frequently does while in A Fib) then the Sense 2 just gives up and won't really check. Even in instances where it was below 120, the Sense will not confirm. I guess we get to settle for inconclusive results instead. Given this feature was the main reason I bought the watch, it may be a deal breaker for me and I may return it for that reason. If this feature is not that important to you, then it may still be a good option.

Overall though, it may be a good option for the right person. If you care primarily about health and fitness tracking and want a good battery life, then this is a good option. At the current $300 price point, I still feel like Fitbit may be asking a little too much given the features of the other higher end options on the market.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Sense 2 Advanced Health and Fitness Smartwatch with Tools to Manage Stress and Sleep, ECG App, SpO2, 24/7 Heart Rate and GPS, Shadow Grey/Graphite, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Marware Revolve Portrait and Landscape Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black (will not fit HDX models) Overall, this is a fine case for the 8.9 inch Fire HD. The overall quality is quite nice - I have other Marware products for my Kindle Touch, and it's good to see that they are continuing to maintain a strong focus on product quality. All the materials feel nice; the stitching is tight and even; there's ample cushioning for tablet protection while maintaining a slim profile; and the elastic strap holds the cover closed in a secure fashion.

I also like how Marware packages their products with a minimum of packaging waste but still ensures the product can travel through the mail without being dinged up. The package is also easy to open - no fuss, no muss.

I initially had some difficulty getting the Fire into the case. The Fire is held in place using a plastic cradle, but it seemed to be too small. I had to (gasp!) resort to reading the user guide that came with it, and found out I needed to position it in a certain way and then snap it in. When it is properly inserted you'll hear and feel a clear "snap" at each of the four corners of the tablet. When properly installed the case holds the tablet very securely. I shook it vigorously (over a thick cushion in case it failed) and the Fire stayed put.

My main quibble is with the rotation feature. I was really looking forward to this since some apps only run in portrait mode; others only in landscape. While the rotation feature works, it is very stiff - you really have to twist hard to get it to rotate. It's a two-handed operation: one hand to rotate the tablet; the other to hold the case while you're turning.

The bottom of the cradle has a tab that fits into a slot on the base of the cover to prop up the tablet. This works in both landscape and portrait modes. There are three tabs so you can adjust the angle.

There are cut outs for the power and HDMI ports. I had no problems accessing any of the ports, power button or volume controls while it was in the cover.

Since I often end up having to charge the Fire while it is in use, I rotated the screen so the power plug is at the top. That allows me to keep the tablet propped up on my desk in landscape mode for video watching, but still use the power cord.

It also offers an auto on/off ability - the Fire turns off when you close the cover, and wakes up when you open the cover. It's a nice feature and it works well.

It has a slot on the cover so you can fit your hand into it for ease of holding it. That has value, but what I would have preferred to have instead (or in addition to) is a pocket on either the inside or the outside to hold items such as a cleaning cloth. This is not a huge problem, but I'll certainly miss that since the case for my original Fire has a outside pouch that is great for holding a cleaning cloth and a small stylus.

I'm going to give this 5 stars, but 4.5 is more accurate given the reluctance of the rotation feature. But, since it does everything else very well, looks good, and feels nice, it's closer to a 5 rating than a 4.
text_fidelity_b: Marware Revolve Portrait and Landscape Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black (will not fit HDX models)

NETGEAR 16-Port Gigabit Ethernet Unmanaged Switch (GS116NA) - Desktop or Wall Mount, and Limited Lifetime Protection I own 2 of these 16 port switches housed in a wiring cabinet in a closet and another, a [[ASIN:B00MPVR50A NETGEAR 8-Port Gigabit Switch (GS108)]] at my computer desk mounted to the wall, and an, [[ASIN:B00MPVR50A NETGEAR 8-Port Gigabit Ethernet Switch (GS108)]] behind the LR TV, then another 3 separate bedroom TV's (kids and my br) have [[ASIN:B002NVOLGI Netgear GS605 5-Port Gigabit Ethernet Switch]] behind them for all the various game systems, video devices etc. I purchased them to upgrade my network from older legacy 10/100 switches a few years back. I have always trusted NETGEAR, mainly because it was used by an old employer of mine. I am very easily able to maintain, GB transfer levels, and all devices on my network are able to pull great speed tests.

I used the switches to segment my network into logical groups, the cabinet, holds the main switch's that run to things like the modem, router, alarm panel, other WiFi AP's, and they connect to my other switches.

One pro tip if you have young kids in the home, make sure and keep the network switches where they (young kids) cannot plug cords into it. At the time my 4 or 5 year old decided he would help dad by plugging the loose end of a cat5 cable into a spare port on the switch. You can guess it wreaked havoc on my system causing crashes etc.

These have held up well to years of use and show no signs of letting me down. I will certainly buy NETGEAR again.

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG Galaxy S9+ Factory Unlocked Smartphone 64GB - Midnight Black I had a Galaxy S4 for several years. It was suitable and did the job. . . mostly. I was having some battery issues and my phone wouldn't update past Android 4.4. I was running into apps that needed a newer version of Android. I could have bought something cheap but I decided to treat myself and found the blue Galaxy S9 on sale for a decent price. I have to say I'm loving this phone.
The 5.8" Quad HD+ Super AMOLED screen is GLORIOUS! I run this is high performance mode with the brightness cranked up. Games, movies, even YouTube and TikTok videos look amazing. The curved edge I worried might be distracting but honestly I only notice in a couple games.
Sound is really good for a cell phone it has stereo speakers. Volume is more than enough.
Performance from the Octa-Core processor and 4GB of ram have not struggled to run anything I've thrown at it.
The camera is great. Maybe struggling a little in very bright light with a light colored subject. Otherwise, night mode gives great low light results. Video shooting is very nice with great slow motion results and a nearly unique super slow-motion recording mode at a mind boggling 960 frames per second is a lot of fun to mess around with.
Battery life is good, I got most of a day is high performance mode and could easily extend it by cutting things back to save battery.
The fingerprint sensor is quick to unlock and easy to use. A trick I found online to improve performance of the fingerprint sensor is to register the same finger more than once. It really works like a charm.
The look is sleek and sophisticated though I'm protecting that glass body with a nice Otterbox Symmetry case. The only real minor negative to the whole thing is this weighs more and is larger than my S4, a little hard on my hands and pocket but really, it's worth it.
I can't express how happy I am with this phone. I'm even buying props and things to use in creative videos and photo shoots.

text_fidelity_a: Phaiser BHS-530 Bluetooth Sport Headset with Mic, Wireless Earbuds for Running, Blackout I have been looking for moderately priced bluetooth headphones for the gym, ones that stayed in place on the treadmill, and offered quality sound. These work so well. Secure fit--the design keeps the headphones in ear without having to constantly re-adjust. Fine sound --rich bass without mush, clear treble without that tinny sound. 3 equalizer modes that allow adjustment- and you can actually hear the difference and choose the one you most enjoy. The controls are easy to use once your fingers know where to press. The call quality through the headphones is very good. The battery life--have used for a few hours over 2-3 weeks and battery life is still "medium" (nice to be told  where the battery life stands each time you turn these on.) Okay, two side comments: they are a bit bulky due to extensive battery life and easy to use controls, but not to the point of hampering fit, and; the memory foam earpieces  did not work that well for me, and when trading them out to try the regular ones, they immediately ripped. No issue, though, cause i preferred the regular earpieces, and had a chance to order more free as well. All in all, a great purchase at a good price.
text_fidelity_b: Phaiser BHS-530 Bluetooth Sport Headset with Mic, Wireless Earbuds for Running, Blackout

text_fidelity_a:
WD_BLACK 1TB SN850 NVMe Internal Gaming SSD Solid State Drive with Heatsink - Works with Playstation 5, Gen4 PCIe, M.2 2280, Up to 7,000 MB/s - WDS100T1XHE I originally bought a WD 2tb NVME to use as my main OS, but it would not migrate/clone properly even with their own software. I downloaded a 3rd party migration/cloning software and that didnt work either. I tried nearly everything I could for 1.5 days! I even tried backing up/restoring manually and then repairing. Nothing worked. It was a complete waste of time. I didnt even learn anything in the process other than learning that I should go with a company that has a readily available comprehensive solution that doesn't needlessly waste your valuable time. 1.5 days down the drain.

So I ended up migrating my Samsung 1tb NVME to a new Samsung 2tb NVME and it couldnt have been any easier. < 15 minutes, very quick! I previously, migrated from a corsair SSD to Samsung 1tb NVME (when i couldnt get another SSD to migrate properly), and that was flawless as well. Why didnt I initially go with the Samsung 2tb instead of WD? Press had positive news about it. I am not a fanboy so I like to try different solutions. That was a mistake. What's apparent to me after this experience is that Samsung is better than all their competitors at providing a comprehensive package of the best hardware and software. The experience is FLAWLESS. I havent had any issues with any of their storage solutions to date.

Why did I bother writing this review? Because I wasted 1.5 days. Something has to come out of it. Maybe itll help someone or maybe WD will get their act together and work on their cloning/migration software because the hardware seems to be fantastic.

Disclosure, I bought and paid for everything myself and I still own HDs/SSDs/MicroSds by WD (only old HDs), Sandisk (microsds, ssds), Seagate (HD), Samsung (SSDs, Micro SDs and NVMEs).
text_fidelity_b: WD_BLACK 1TB SN850 NVMe Internal Gaming SSD Solid State Drive with Heatsink - Works with Playstation 5, Gen4 PCIe, M.2 2280, Up to 7,000 MB/s - WDS100T1XHE
